note: Hoax threats move from airliners to newsrooms; Putin confirms Abu Dhabi talks for Tuesday; the US strikes Qeshm again; Belgium's King keeps De Wever.

weather.now: About 3 °C at dawn, dry, a light south-south-east wind; fog in the south clearing to sun; no warnings in force [1, 2]
weather.tomorrow: Sun cloudy but almost dry, 5–10 °C, south-west wind 3; a shower possible in the afternoon
weather.weekNote: Dry and about 10 °C to Tuesday, with fog at times; from Wednesday changeable and milder, with rain heavy at times on Thursday. KNMI for 13–20 Nov: “Wisselvallig met temperaturen rond het langjarig gemiddelde.” [3, 1]

items.t: Fog clearing to sun, about 10 °C; GLOW Eindhoven's free light walk runs from 18:30. [1, 4]
Canes host Chicago at 02:00 CET Sunday in the new “Hometown Remix” jersey. [5]
DIY DesignMarkt in Köln-Ehrenfeld, 12:00–18:00; the children's show at Kasteel Hoensbroek. [6, 7]

five.t: **Hoax bomb threats hit at least 17 more flights and emptied Ireland's broadcaster;** NATO sent Hungarian Gripens up three times and a KLM flight was checked at Schiphol.
**Putin confirms trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday;** Umerov leads Ukraine's team, and ballistic missiles hit Kyiv overnight.
**The US strikes an Iranian air-defence site on Qeshm, its first strike since the midterms;** Trump: “We do minor strikes,” as Tehran weighs a Qatari two-day plan.
**King Philippe rejects De Wever's resignation;** budget talks restart Monday, and the Prime Minister reports back on 16 Nov.
**US payrolls rose 165,000 against 65,000 expected;** a December Fed hike is priced at about 78%, and USD/EUR fixed at 0.8957, the best rate of the week.

pick.t: If you read one thing: the HCSS paper. It names JFC Brunssum and 1 German-Netherlands Corps as the pilot for a European command chain to act when the North Atlantic Council cannot.

items.h: Putin confirms trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday as missiles hit Kyiv
items.body: President Putin told his Security Council on 6 Nov: “Trilateral talks on the Ukrainian issue will be held in the United Arab Emirates next week, on Tuesday,” with Vladimir Medinsky leading Russia's delegation. [9] Davyd Arakhamia said in Washington that Rustem Umerov heads Ukraine's team: “No, it's Umerov.” [10] Adviser Serhii Leshchenko said Ukraine proposes “halting the fighting where the front line currently stands”. [11] Missile waves hit Kyiv from just before 23:00 to 03:30, wounding at least three including a child; the Komyshuvakha toll rose to 50. [12, 13]
items.next: Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Tue 10 Nov [9]; the Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin on 19 Nov.

items.h: US strikes an Iranian air-defence site on Qeshm as Tehran weighs a Qatari plan
items.body: Iranian state media reported two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island on 6 Nov, the first US strike since the 3 Nov midterms; President Trump: “We do minor strikes,” and “we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five.” [14] Two officials told AP that Iran is reviewing a Qatari two-day plan: the US lifts its blockade and releases some frozen funds, inspectors enter bombed sites, then Iran reopens Hormuz. [14] The Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines; UKMTO reported an explosion on a tanker leaving the strait. [15] In Yemen at least 30 people were killed at a market in Taiz, which the Houthis blame on Saudi airstrikes and the government on Houthi missiles. [16]
items.next: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris on 9–10 Nov; no date is set for US–Iran talks. [15]

items.h: Eleven PLA sorties near Taiwan, nine across the median line; Taipei leaves Papua New Guinea
items.body: Taiwan's defence ministry counted 11 Chinese military aircraft sorties, nine of which crossed the median line, plus 10 navy ships and three official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 7 Nov, against three sorties a day earlier. [17] The foreign ministry said on 6 Nov that it will close its representative office in Papua New Guinea, accusing China of using “political pressure and economic influence to interfere in other countries' diplomatic decisions.” [18] KCNA reported a plenary meeting of the Supreme People's Assembly Standing Committee on 7 Nov. [19]
items.next: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov; Taiwan holds local elections on 28 Nov.

items.h: Sudan's army and RSF dispute four North Kordofan villages; 24 killed near Beni
items.body: The army-allied Joint Force said it took Umm Samima, Kazqil, Al-Hamadi and Abu Qud west and south of El Obeid on 5 Nov; Rapid Support Forces (RSF) videos claim it still holds them. [20] UN agencies said on 6 Nov that 15.4 million Sudanese need shelter; the IOM's Mohamed Refaat: “our warehouses are completely empty now.” [21] In eastern Congo fighting spread on the Kashebere–Kibati road in North Kivu, and a civil-society official said 24 civilians were killed near Beni overnight into 6 Nov. [22, 23] In Niamey on 6 Nov Niger's and Mali's leaders said they had “réitéré leur ferme détermination à éradiquer le terrorisme”, reiterated their determination to eradicate terrorism. [24]
items.next: The Sudan–South Sudan joint political and security mechanism meets in Khartoum on 8–10 Nov. [25]

items.h: Colom's lead in Mississippi grows to 2,574; Alaska has about 60,000 ballots left
items.body: AP had Scott Colom 2,574 votes ahead of Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith on Friday afternoon, up from 1,882; Hyde-Smith: “We are not backing down. This election is not over.” [26] In Alaska Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by 637 votes, 48% to 47.7%, with about 60,000 ballots uncounted. [27]
items.next: Mississippi mail ballots must arrive by 10 Nov and counties certify by 13 Nov; Alaska tabulates ranked-choice ballots on 18 Nov. [26, 27]

feature.title: Sudan's grid under drones: 15 power stations in 13 days
body: Between 20 Oct and 1 Nov drones hit about 15 power stations in 10 of Sudan's 18 states, Asharq Al-Awsat counted; the five Darfur states, held by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), were not hit. [28] The government and the Emergency Lawyers group blame the RSF, which generally does not comment. [29]

The targets run the length of the grid. On 26 Oct five stations in Jazira, Gedaref and White Nile were struck, and an official reported “power outages across large parts of these three states”. [30] Um Dabakir at Kosti, the largest thermal plant at 500 MW, lost four transformers and shut on 28–29 Oct. On 1 Nov the Abu Hamad substation was destroyed and River Nile State lost power, and a guard was killed at Al-Dabbah. [29] On 2–3 Nov drones reached New Halfa and Aroma in Kassala and the Al-Ghazali substation near Merowe. [31]

Generation fell from 4,400 MW before the war to 1,100 MW before the October strikes, and the Merowe Dam's 1,250 MW supplies more than 70% of what is left, an employee of the state electricity holding company told AP. [29] A UN spokesperson said on 27 Oct that “the attacks threaten the stability of the national electricity grid”. [32] Sudan's Sovereignty Council told the UN it counted 70 attacks with 187 drones launched from Ethiopia between 15 Feb and 27 Oct, naming Asosa, Kurmuk and Bahir Dar; Ethiopia denies it. [33] Former energy minister Adel Ibrahim told Asharq that only Merowe, Atbara and Maranjan remain as main stations, and that “complete darkness will engulf the country” if the strikes go on. [28]

incidents.place: Europe: at least 17 flights (CZ, FR, IT, PT, HU, BG, DK, NL); marker at Prague
incidents.text: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 17 flights by midday GMT, nine of them to or from Prague; four aircraft over France landed at Orly and Bordeaux, and a KLM flight from Prague was checked at Schiphol. No explosives were found. [34, 35, 36]

incidents.place: Dublin: RTÉ, Newstalk, Irish Independent; also Sky News (UK), Nova TV (BG); marker at Donnybrook
incidents.text: An email headed “MESSAGE TO THE WEST” threatened newsrooms in Ireland and the UK; RTÉ's Donnybrook campus, Newstalk and the Irish Independent were evacuated. [37, 38]

incidents.place: Lithuania: sites not named (marker at Vilnius)
incidents.text: Lithuania's State Security Department expelled three Ukrainians it says took paid tasks from hostile foreign services via Telegram, including filming sites; no criminal case was opened. [39]

leads.title: Hoax bomb threats hit 17 more flights and empty Ireland's broadcaster
leads.teaser: A fourth day of airliner threats brought fighter escorts over Hungary and a check at Schiphol, and an emailed threat emptied RTÉ. Nothing has been found anywhere.
rows: On 6 Nov threats hit at least 17 flights by midday GMT; Prague police counted nine flights to or from Prague, and the French prime minister's office reported “four new bomb threats” against aircraft over France. [34, 35]

A KLM flight from Prague was checked at Schiphol, about 180 km from Heerlen; the Royal Marechaussee: “Er zijn geen explosieven aangetroffen aan boord”, no explosives on board. [36] Hungarian Gripens escorted three airliners. [40]

An email headed “MESSAGE TO THE WEST” emptied RTÉ, Newstalk and the Irish Independent. Tánaiste Simon Harris: “Any attack or threat of attack on the media is a threat and attack on our democracy.” [37]
A0. Taoiseach Micheál Martin: the threats “just illustrate how relatively simple it can be to cause disruption and to undermine the normal operation of society.” [35] Moscow denies involvement. [34]
leads.sw: Each hoax costs a fighter sortie, a diversion or an evacuation and costs the sender an email: test baseline requirements 6 and 7 (civil communications, civil transportation) by asking who handles a threat against a flight into Maastricht Aachen or against L1's studios, and how JFC Brunssum hears of it.

leads.title: The Dutch security coordinator warns digital resilience is falling behind
leads.teaser: The Cybersecuritybeeld Nederland 2026 puts the gap from a known flaw to its exploitation at a few hours, as the cold-chain attacks go on.
rows: The National Coordinator for Counterterrorism and Security (NCTV) published the Cybersecuritybeeld Nederland 2026 on 6 Nov: “De kans op spionage, datadiefstal, sabotage en uitval van digitale processen groeit en dit is zeer zorgelijk”, the risk of espionage, data theft, sabotage and outages is growing and very worrying. The gap between finding a vulnerability and exploiting it is now a few hours. [41]
No new store incident on 6 Nov; NOS reports Delhaize was hit again earlier in the week and that Ahold Delhaize's attack last month cost €200–250 million in revenue. [42]
leads.sw: The host nation's own assessment is the baseline for JFC Brunssum's resilience reporting: requirements 1 and 6 (continuity of government, civil communications) now turn on patch times measured in hours.

pattern: **From aircraft to newsrooms:** on the day of a fourth wave of airliner threats, an emailed threat emptied RTÉ and reached Sky News and Nova TV. [37, 43]
**Fighters as the answer:** NATO ordered Hungarian Gripens up three times in hours to escort threatened airliners. [40]
**The method named, the actor not:** Spain's foreign minister calls it “hybrid aggression” and the Irish government a co-ordinated campaign; no government has attributed it. [43, 38]
tracker: NATO orders Hungarian Gripens to escort three threatened airliners
Irish police, Defence Forces and cyber authorities open an investigation into the media threats
The NCTV publishes the Cybersecuritybeeld Nederland 2026
Lithuania expels three Ukrainians over paid tasks for hostile services
EUCOM's “See Something, Do Something” vigilance campaign
indicators: At least 17 flights on 6 Nov; Thursday revised to at least 30
RTÉ, Newstalk and the Irish Independent evacuated on 6 Nov
Drones near JOA-C military and logistics nodes
Lithuania: the Kaliningrad border is “calmer” than Poland's
hybrid.note: Within 100 km of Heerlen there is no new case; the nearest event in the window is the KLM flight checked at Schiphol, about 180 km away. [36]

europe.h: King Philippe rejects De Wever's resignation and sends him back to the budget
europe.body: On 6 Nov the palace said the King decided “to reject the prime minister's resignation” and asked him to “resume budget negotiations immediately”; the coalition leaders “reaffirmed their determination to reach an agreement on a sound budgetary path for the next three years.” [44] De Wever meets each deputy prime minister from Mon 9 Nov and reports to the King on 16 Nov; N-VA chair Valerie Van Peel: “Het is met z'n allen erdoor of z'n allen onderuit”, we all get through it or we all go down. [45]
europe.sw: SHAPE's and NATO headquarters' host stays on provisional twelfths until a budget passes, which holds new Belgian defence commitments at this year's level.

europe.h: Lithuania expels three Ukrainians paid to film sites for hostile services
europe.body: Lithuania's State Security Department (VSD) said on 5 Nov that three Ukrainians took paid tasks from “hostile” foreign services, briefed over Telegram; the interior minister said they were “carrying out various assigned tasks for payment, such as filming specific sites”. They are barred for five years and no criminal case was opened. [39]
europe.sw: Paid, Telegram-tasked filming of sites is reconnaissance: ask the J2 whether Vilnius shares the list of filmed sites, since some may sit on JFC Brunssum's reinforcement routes.

countries.h: NATO scrambles Hungarian Gripens three times in hours over hoax bomb threats
countries.body: On 6 Nov NATO ordered Gripens already airborne on a training flight to escort an Airbus A321 flying Brussels–Sofia from 09:48, then two aircraft out of Prague bound for Cyprus and Bucharest from 10:33, until each left Hungarian airspace; no device was reported. [40, 46] Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi: “A légtér biztonsága folyamatos figyelmet és azonnali reagálást követel”, airspace security demands constant attention and an immediate response. [46]
countries.sw: NATO air policing now answers hoaxes against civil flights over a priority country: baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation) is being tested at the cost of fighter hours.

countries.h: Brussels gives Slovakia no exemption from the 2027 migration solidarity pool
countries.body: The Commission's annual migration report, published on 6 Nov, gives Slovakia no exemption for 2027 and says it “should pay a contribution”; member states settle the pool by qualified majority in the Council. KDH MEP Miriam Lexmann: “Všetky krajiny, ktoré si o výnimku požiadali, okrem Slovenska, ju dostali”, every country that asked got the exemption except Slovakia. [47]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 3 (uncontrolled movement of people): Slovakia hosts tens of thousands of Ukrainian refugees and argues for border-protection money instead of payments.

countries.h: Germany pledges €200 million more for Ukraine's winter as Wadephul flies to Warsaw
countries.body: Leaving for Warsaw on 6 Nov, Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said: “Es geht um Krieg oder Frieden: Die Zukunft unseres Miteinanders in Europa entscheidet sich in der Ukraine”, it is about war or peace, and Europe's future is being decided in Ukraine. He announced “weitere 200 Millionen Euro”, a further €200 million for energy, heating and humanitarian aid, and listed shadow-fleet tankers, undersea damage, aircraft bomb threats, cyberattacks on food retailers and drones as attempts to unsettle Europe. [48]
countries.sw: Berlin's list matches the set the J9 tracks against baseline requirements 2, 4, 6 and 7, named in one statement by Germany's foreign minister.

countries.h: Pistorius: about 190,000 troops, and no conscription needed if the trend holds
countries.body: Defence Minister Boris Pistorius told the Funke group on 7 Nov that about 190,000 soldiers now serve, the most in 13 years: “Wenn sich der Kurs fortsetzt, haben wir keine Aufwuchsprobleme”, if the trend continues we will have no problem growing. [49] The law in force since January restored medical screening and conscript registration and targets 255,000–270,000 personnel by 2035; dpa gives the starting figure as about 184,000. [50]
countries.sw: A larger Bundeswehr without conscription keeps Germany's host-nation and reinforcement roles staffed; the screening data are the planning base for the 2035 target.

euregio.h: Provincial parties question the airport's losses before the Schiphol sale
euregio.body: L1 puts the sale of 40% of Maastricht Aachen Airport to Schiphol at about €4.2 million; in 2025 the airport handled 41,600 tonnes of cargo and 159,000 passengers against targets of 171,000 tonnes and 470,000. [51] D66 group leader Wesseling: “Het is zorgelijk dat de provincie ooit zo'n desinvestering heeft gedaan”, it is worrying that the province ever made such a loss-making investment. [52]
euregio.fy: Nothing changes for flights; the Provinciale Staten vote before the end of the year.

euregio.h: A bus strike disrupts about half of LeTec lines around Verviers on Monday
euregio.body: The CSC union's strike on Mon 9 Nov at the private operators running LeTec lines covers Verviers, Visé, Aywaille, Spa, Waimes, Saint-Vith and La Calamine, among others; spokesperson Isabelle Tasset: “les premières informations laissent présager des perturbations importantes”, early information points to major disruption. [53]
euregio.fy: Do not count on TEC buses in the Liège–Verviers area or the East Cantons on Monday.

euregio.h: Aachen's Krefelder Straße is closed after a district-heating pipe failed
euregio.body: Police closed Krefelder Straße towards the city centre at about 20:00 on 5 Nov after a district-heating pipe failed; it was still shut on the morning of 6 Nov, with no reopening time. [54]
euregio.fy: Allow extra time entering Aachen from the north until the police reopen it.

items.h: Rutte tells the IEA chief NATO will help protect energy infrastructure
items.body: Meeting International Energy Agency (IEA) Executive Director Fatih Birol and the North Atlantic Council on 5 Nov, Secretary General Mark Rutte said that “without fuel, we cannot move” and “without secure infrastructure, there is no energy at all.” NATO will keep building its capacity to help nations protect critical energy and undersea infrastructure. [55]
items.sw: Energy is baseline requirement 2: a NATO energy-protection role gives the J9 a counterpart at headquarters for host-nation energy questions.

items.h: Germany leads more than 6,000 troops in two Lithuanian exercises to 3 Dec
items.body: Freedom Shield 26-II at Rūdninkai and Grand Eagle 26 at the Gen. Silvestras Žukauskas training area run from 6 Nov to 3 Dec with Germany's 45th Armoured Brigade “Lietuva”, the 37th Mechanised Infantry Brigade and Multinational Brigade Lithuania contingents from the Netherlands, Norway, the Czech Republic, Croatia, Belgium and Luxembourg. Convoys move from Kalvarija on 6–7 Nov and from Klaipėda port on 10–12 Nov. [56]
items.sw: Convoys on Lithuanian roads and out of Klaipėda exercise baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation) inside JFC Brunssum's area, with Dutch and Belgian troops in the brigade.

items.h: Lithuania says its Kaliningrad border is “calmer” than Poland's
items.body: Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas said on 6 Nov: “the situation on the border with Kaliningrad is certainly calmer than it was in Poland.” Lithuanian troops have supported border guards since 8 Oct, a deployment that runs to mid-November. [57]
items.sw: The Kaliningrad line is the hinge of JFC Brunssum's area; the troop support to Lithuania's border guards is the civil-military arrangement to watch when it lapses in mid-November.

items.h: Kratos wins a Valkyrie production order and plans to triple its jet-engine line
items.body: Kratos reported third-quarter revenue of $471.8 million, up 35.7%, and a record backlog of $2.650 billion on 5 Nov. [58] Chief executive Eric DeMarco on the call: “we have now very recently received what I will call a Valkyrie low-rate initial production, or LRIP, contract award,” and he plans to “approximately triple the manufacturing capacity” of the Oklahoma City engine line by the end of 2027, for up to 3,000 small turbojets in 2027. [59]
items.sw: Cheap turbojets at thousands a year power small cruise missiles and jet drones, the same class Ukraine stopped only 66% of the time in October when Russia flew them. [60]

items.h: A Czech-owned firm qualifies for the Army's $4.2 billion ammunition-plant framework
items.body: CSG said on 6 Nov that its MSM North America unit was selected to compete for task orders under a five-year Army framework with a ceiling of about $4.2 billion to modernise seven government-owned plants, among them Holston, Radford, Lake City and Iowa. MSM is separately building a $635 million artillery complex at Iowa due in 2029, with capacity for up to 36,000 155 mm rounds a month. [61]
items.sw: European ownership inside US shell production ties allied 155 mm supply to the same plants that refill US stocks.

items.h: The Pentagon picks Machina to build airframes for LUCAS, its Shahed copy
items.body: Machina was selected on 6 Nov to develop and qualify a “RoboCrafted airframe” for the Low-Cost Unmanned Combat Attack System (LUCAS), built by SpektreWorks, and to deploy two pilot “Edge Factories” that make airframes in the field; no value was disclosed. LUCAS saw its first combat use in the Iran war. [62]
items.sw: Expeditionary drone factories change what a host nation may be asked to support: power, space and security for a production cell, not just a depot.

ttp.title: Week in war, 2–7 Nov: robots carry the load, nets catch the fibre drones
body: Ukraine's defence ministry counted 31,398 ground-robot missions in October, a record and about 4.2 times January's 7,511; most were logistics, the rest casualty evacuation, strike, mining and drone launch. [63] Russian channels claimed on 6 Nov to have repelled a 28-robot assault near Lyman, which Ukraine has not confirmed. Against fibre-optic first-person-view (FPV) drones, which jamming cannot stop, Phantom Defense's Mangal net-launcher reacts in 0.2 seconds and detects an FPV at about 40 m against trees; ten systems are in combat trials and two attacks have been repelled, by the developer's count. [64]

In the air the problem is speed. The General Staff counted 6,473 Shahed-type drones in October and destroyed 75%, but only 66% of the jet-powered ones against 89% of the propeller models; the ministry counted 2,688 jet Shahed-238s, up from 1,935 in September. [60] The ministry adds: “Ballistics, which the enemy actively used to hit civilian infrastructure, remains a separate challenge.” [60] A Shahed downed on 4 Nov carried leaflets with a QR code that Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert Brovdi called “a cyber-phishing trap activated when scanning a QR code.” [65] Russian crews now hang ambush drones on high-voltage power lines, a Ukrainian technique copied. [66]

Deep strikes hit aircraft on the ground: Russia lost at least 11 aircraft and two helicopters in October, its worst month since Operation Spiderweb, including four Su-34s at Borisoglebsk to Neptune missiles. [67] On the Russian side Rostec showed a mobile ZAK-30 airburst gun on a three-axle truck that detects drones at up to 2 km and engages them at 1,000–1,300 m. [68]

items.h: Meta ships specialised Muse models that forget 2.4 times less
items.body: Meta began rolling out specialised models trained with what it calls Muse Wonder, with Active Memory and Active Focus, to all Muse and Meta AI users on 6 Nov. Its internal evaluations: a Personal Superintelligence Index of 47% against 38% for the previous model, 90% on its Active Memory evaluation against 76%, and “a 2.4x reduction in forgetting critical information.” [69] The same day it launched Spaces, agent-built trackers and planners that update in the background. [70]

items.h: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small: 86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro Hard
items.body: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Small on 5 Nov, a mixture-of-experts model with 594 billion parameters, 17 billion active, that takes images and returns text; it reports 86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 (Hard) and 81.6% on MMMU Pro, at $0.30 per million input tokens and $1.00 per million output tokens. The company says it will publish the weights under Apache 2.0 “next week”. [71] Artificial Analysis scores it 31 on its index, level with Gemini 3.8 Flash at about a sixth of the cost per task. [72]

items.h: METR finds Anthropic's internal progress running 1.9 times faster than before October 2025
items.body: METR published an independent assessment on 5 Nov: Anthropic's internal benchmark scores are improving about 1.9 times faster than before October 2025 (95% interval 1.5–2.8), against 1.4 times across other developers, and METR guesses “a majority (perhaps ≈80%)” of the acceleration is due to AI. It notes: “Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative for these conclusions,” and Anthropic cancelled the compute-verification part of the contract. [73]

cards.n: Nearly two dozen US dead, 11 in combat; cost above $47 billion by 28 Oct. [74, 75]
Nothing reported on the Europe option sets; the review ends in December. [76]
Stopgap expires 11 Dec; AEI's Todd Harrison: “zero chance” of appropriations. [77]
German-led Freedom Shield and Grand Eagle, 6 Nov – 3 Dec. [56]

words.where: Meeting with IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol, NATO headquarters
words.quote: without secure infrastructure, there is no energy at all
words.context: One of four lines on energy and defence; he also said “without reliable supply chains, we cannot ramp up our defence industrial production.” [55]

words.role: Commander, US European Command, and SACEUR
words.where: Launch of EUCOM's “See Something, Do Something” campaign
words.quote: By embracing a proactive security mindset and enhancing collective vigilance, we build a stronger force protection environment that keeps us safe and ready.
words.context: EUCOM asks troops and families to vary routines; Germany has raised its Russian sabotage threat level to “substantial”. Reported by Defense News on 6 Nov. [78]

dod.h: A Republican chairman says there are “a lot of questions about Hegseth”
dod.body: House Oversight Chairman James Comer said on 6 Nov there are “a lot of questions about Hegseth” and “We have no idea what the strategy is moving forward in Iran”; President Trump says he has “every intention” of keeping the Secretary. [79] Rep. Thomas Massie will reintroduce eight impeachment articles when the House returns on 9 Nov, with a privileged resolution that forces a vote within two days: “There is one contingency in which I won't reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns.” [77] No delivery of the Europe force options due on 6 Nov has been reported. [76]
dod.sw: A forced vote in the week the Europe options reach the Secretary puts the posture review's decision-maker under a clock; the 76,000-troop floor in law binds whatever he picks.

dod.h: The Iran war has cost 866 US wounded and more than $47 billion
dod.body: Nearly two dozen US service members have died in the Iran war, 11 in combat, and 866 have been wounded, with interceptor stocks depleted and hundreds of base facilities damaged, Stars and Stripes reported on 6 Nov; Central Command's Adm. Brad Cooper: “no one could have imagined the trajectory of events that we would be on.” [74] The Pentagon put the cost above $47 billion on 28 Oct. [75]
dod.sw: Interceptors fired in CENTCOM are interceptors missing from European stocks, and refilling them competes with EUCOM's air-defence lines in the same budget.

news.h: EUCOM asks troops and families to vary routines as hybrid threats mount
news.body: European Command's “See Something, Do Something” campaign, launched on 3 Nov, asks personnel and families to vary routines and report suspicious activity; Gen. Grynkewich called them “our most precious asset”. Germany has raised its Russian sabotage threat level to “substantial”, and more than 30,000 US personnel serve there. [78]
news.sw: The US element at Brunssum falls under the same campaign: brief families this week on varying routines and on where to report.

news.h: The Army renames its cooks “tactical field feeding specialists”
news.body: Military occupational specialty 92G is now titled tactical field feeding specialist, with the code unchanged; Col. Stacy Moore-Callaway, the Quartermaster commandant: “we do it because the character of war has changed.” [80]
news.sw: Feeding troops under drone observation is a sustainment problem in every exercise in our area; ask whether 92G training now covers it.

congress.h: Congress returns Monday with five weeks to fund the government
congress.body: The continuing resolution expires on 11 Dec; Capital Alpha's Byron Callan puts a shutdown at 50% and a reconciliation bill at 10%, and AEI's Todd Harrison said: “There's zero chance of appropriations getting passed because that requires 60 votes in the Senate.” [77] Forecast International expects another stopgap into 2027 and calls reconciliation, with about $54 billion for autonomous warfare and $17 billion for Golden Dome, “likely off the table”. [81] No new action on H.R. 8800 or on Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral's USAREUR-AF nomination.
congress.sw: The autonomy money sits in reconciliation, not the base bill: without it, AUTOWARCOM's first year rests on reprogramming.

items.h: TRICARE's 2027 costs rise for Select families; open season opens Monday
items.body: Active-duty families pay no enrollment fee and no Prime deductible in 2027; the TRICARE Select Group B family deductible for E-5 and above rises from $397 to $411, the Group A family primary-care copay from $28 to $30, and the Group B catastrophic cap from $1,324 to $1,372, with pharmacy costs unchanged. [82] Open season runs 9 Nov – 8 Dec. [83] The 2027 retirement-plan limits are still unpublished. [84]
items.fy: If the family is on Select, compare it with Prime Overseas before 8 Dec; hold January TSP changes until the 2027 limits appear.

dates: TRICARE and Federal Benefits open seasons open
2027 pay raise and TRICARE cost changes take effect
career.note: Priority topics with nothing in the window: AUTOWARCOM (no commander named) and special operations; no remarks found from Caine, Telle or LaNeve.

research.title: How Europe can act when NATO cannot: From NATO 3.0 to a European Plan B
research.authors: Pieter-Jan Vandoren and Davis Ellison, with Nico Tak and Tim Sweijs
summary: The paper starts from “NATO 3.0”, the division of labour in which European Allies take primary responsibility for conventional deterrence and the United States remains the ultimate backstop. The authors argue this assumes Washington stays a cooperative Ally, and that Europeans must also plan for a case where US political choices block consensus in the North Atlantic Council (NAC). Europe, they write, already has much of the force and command it needs: “What is currently missing is a clear, pre-agreed and practiced European political-strategic chain that connects political authority to military action.” [85]

They set out a strict NATO-first sequence. Plan A1 is a full transatlantic operation, Plan A2 a European-led NATO operation under the NAC and SACEUR, and Plan B applies only when the NAC cannot authorise one. Plan B rests on a European Defence Compact, a master treaty with regional protocols, and a European Compact Council of European Allies, including non-EU members, acting as “what the NAC is to NATO”. Authority would run through a European Strategic Commander to a designated Joint Force Command using the same regional plans: “Plan B changes the source of political authority, not the geography, standards or route back to NATO.” A supremacy clause hands the operation back to SACEUR once the NAC acts, and the authors insist the chain is credible only if exercised in advance. [85]
findings: **Three regions, one design:** the Compact has one master treaty and three regional protocols (North, Centre, South); every plan uses one supported and two supporting Joint Force Commands. [85]
**A precedent at SHAPE:** the European Strategic Commander could sit at SHAPE under a NAC-approved access arrangement, as LIVE OAK did after its creation in 1959 and move to SHAPE in 1961. [85]

**Land command:** France, Germany and Poland should each prepare a multinational three-star headquarters able to command up to three corps; US Army Europe and Africa exercised that role under JFC Brunssum in Avenger Triad 24. [85]
**Brunssum as the pilot:** “JFC Brunssum and 1 German-Netherlands Corps offer one suitable pairing”; France, Germany and the UK should convene willing Allies within three months. [85]
research.method: A conceptual design paper built on treaty texts (Washington Treaty Articles 5, 8 and 9; EU Treaty Articles 42(7) and 43(1)), historical precedents (the 1954 Brussels Treaty, LIVE OAK, Berlin Plus) and existing NATO command structures. It has no data, modelling or costings, so it cannot show whether capitals would sign or how Washington would respond; the authors concede “The Compact cannot eliminate this risk” of escalation within NATO. The title page calls the publication “AI-driven”, with the authors responsible; it was funded under the Dutch ministries' PROGRESS framework.
research.sw: The paper offers our own headquarters and 1 German-Netherlands Corps as the test bed: ask how host-nation-support arrangements in the Joint Operations Area would carry over if the mandate came from a European council rather than the NAC.

aperture.contrarian: The airliner hoaxes read as a Russian campaign, and Spain's foreign minister says “It is clear that this is no coincidence.” [43] The other read: no device has been found, the one arrest at Schiphol was a passenger threatening his own flight, and a copycat needs only an email. [86]
aperture.weak: Drones took down Sudan's grid station by station in the same weeks Ukraine logged 31,398 ground-robot missions in a month: unmanned systems now carry both the attack on infrastructure and the logistics. [29, 63] Confirmation would be a European grid operator budgeting drone defence for substations.

otd.title: On this day · 7 November 1944
otd.body: At Kommerscheidt, across the Kall gorge from Vossenack in the Hürtgen Forest, German forces including the 116th Panzer Division counterattacked the 112th Infantry of the US 28th Infantry Division; by the end of the day the defenders had been pushed out of the village and fell back to the woods, while engineers cleared the rest of Vossenack. The survivors withdrew across the Kall on 8 November. Kommerscheidt is about 40 km from Heerlen. [119, 120]

culture.title: Weckmann: the Rhineland's St Martin's bread
culture.body: After Wednesday's Martinszug, Rhineland children are handed a Weckmann, a yeast-dough figure holding a clay pipe: “Im Rheinland ist es Tradition, dass Kinder nach dem Martinsumzug einen Weckmann geschenkt bekommen.” The pipe replaced a bishop's staff to make the figure secular, and the bake has “allein im Rheinland mehr als 50 verschiedene Namen”, from Stutenkerl to Dambedei. [121] Köln opens carnival at 11:11 the same day. [122]
